utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecution appreciates you doing that. However, if you don't mind, if I can point out the sections of the report just so we can make this efficient instead of struggling around the report, the Prosecution would be willing to do that too, so we're not talking about things in the abstract. And just so -- while I'm up, the Prosecution does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whatever the answer is, you will offer to present to the Chamber or hint at the relevant portions in the report where what is found here in the summary, whether in the right place or not, is substantiated. That offer, Mr. Jordash, would only create clarity, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It would, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That offer is accepted. We'll hear then from you, I take it on Monday. Meanwhile Mr. Jordash can ask questions and use his time as he wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before ending the day, we just do have one brief submission with respect to 1D1375 before the weekend starts and materials are provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Given the time, could I put another proposition to Mr. Theunens and ask him to consider that over the weekend too. I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We're all relaxing over the weekend, Mr. Theunens, and you are the one who has to work hard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's for the just cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The proposition is this. It is picking up where we left off with the Arkan document. We dealt, as Your Honours know, with nine documents and there are in other sections documents which deal with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And our proposition to you, Mr. Theunens, is that the only document which deal and mention connection with Arkan and the DB is P327, P1077, and P1192 and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have had you an opportunity to write it down, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm doing it as we speak, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, could you please repeat before you waste the whole of the weekend on the wrong numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I wanted Mr. Theunens to repeat so that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And my question to you is, is that the basis upon which you concluded that the DB had a connection with Arkan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. It's mischaracterising his conclusion. He says the MUP of Serbia. There are many, many, many, many more documents that reference the MUP of Serbia. So to put it to him accurately, just so it is the context of what his actual opinion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Keeping in mind, what we could do is we could also invite the parties to phrase the question -- that Mr. Jordash phrases the question that you look at it. I'm not in a position at this moment to finally determine whether there's any misrepresentation in it. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I could point Your Honour to the conclusion in due course where Mr. Theunens, in fact, says, "Ministry of the Interior (including the DB)." And I'll find that any moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution can makes its quick submission if it is an efficient use of late court time right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's right -- it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash will seek his lines and meanwhile you may make a submission, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found it already. Then let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Chapter 1, page --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which section?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Chapter 1, page 105, and it's little D. Intelligence reports by JNA security organs drafted between October 1991 and January 1992 on Zeljko Raznjatovic, aka Arkan, and his Serbian Volunteer Guard, can confirm the close relations between Arkan and the MUP, including the state security, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now this line first, Mr. Theunens, needs some clarification. Did you want to say confirm the close relations between Arkan and the MUP and then give as a fact that the state security of Serbia, the SDB, is part of the MUP; or did you want to express here that these documents, apart from confirming the close relations between Arkan and the MUP, also confirm that the state security of Serbia joined in that close relationship? Specifically, that part of the MUP, of the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is your second proposition, Your Honours, and okay, we can just -- I mean, under that title or that section or that introduction, a number of documents are cited. And, for example, P327 clearly mentions SDB of Serbia. For example. I haven't gone through the others yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is one of the three that was just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now what apparently Mr. Jordash is very much interested in to know is whether, apart from these three documents, whether you found in other documents clear keys to not only a relationship with the MUP --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but also specifically with the SDB, as a part of the MUP. That is apparently the question. And I -- I would -- I would ask you whether you could consider that over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Prosecution doesn't object to the question as the Chamber just phrased it. That was different than Mr. Jordash's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just -- everyone is happy now with the way I phrased it, apparently. I listened to you Mr. Weber and I listened to Mr. Jordash and I'm happy that was able to phrase the question in such a way that everyone goes into the weekend with a happy mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apart from the excerpt on Monday, from the Butler report, that is the end of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat this? The --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Butler [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one you wanted to give for a full review so that you have this one minute after the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a hard copy so that -- Mr. Theunens, would be you willing to read that, I do understand, ten-page document?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this relates to our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Then please make your submission, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, 1D1375 is an excerpt, as Mr. Jordash just referenced, 11-page excerpt that is from a 138-page report. We got extraordinarily late notice of this document. I did have the opportunity during this very session to first review this document. There are many things in the 138 pages, including discussions of Red Berets, use of MUP units, that are relevant to this case. We leave it to the Defence if they want to use it, but the Prosecution, based on the severely late notice that was received, we would then ask for wide latitude -- one, we'd ask -- we object to notice. We maintain our objection. We believe if the Chamber's going to overrule our objection, that the witness should actually get all 138 pages, not just a selected 10- or 11-page excerpt and then we ask for wide latitude if our objection is overruled to go into matters that may be referenced in that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm, first of all, a practical person. Are the 138 pages available?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We can make them available within a short time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I suggest that what consequences to attach to the late notice, of course, very much depends on what you and you what want to do the ten pages, the 138 pages. First of all, Mr. Theunens, I don't know your programme, ten pages suddenly become 138. Would you be willing -- if Mr. Jordash could already indicate which ten pages he will focus on, and if you would then try to acquaint yourself with at least the main lines of what appears in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: For us it not the ten pages. It is simply the paragraph that we wanted to put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Theunens, Mr. Jordash will provide the 138 pages. He will indicate which ones -- which ten he had already, ready in translation in an earlier stage so you know that that was -- is what Mr. Weber got at the time, and then he'll also indicate which specific paragraph he is interested in, and if you would be willing to read certainly the ten pages but, to the extent possible, also the remaining 128, that would be highly appreciated, and I know that I put a heavy burden on your shoulders. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We maintain our objection, first and foremost. That being said, based on what the transcript reflects today, the question's going to be put to him something to the effect to comment on whether he agrees or disagrees with an expert opinion. So we believe that we should have wide latitude in the scope of that opinion that's being expressed in that 138 pages to explore whatever area Mr. Theunens's opinion in this case is in agreement or disagreement with the contents of that report and the documents cited. So although the Defence might want to pick out a very small portion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me -- Mr. Jordash, if in the document, which you give notice of at a very late stage, if Mr. Weber finds therein other relevant matters, then I would expect you not to object too easily on going through the context of.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the proper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And again, let me -- I'll follow my usual line. Mr. Weber, I know exactly what I'm going to expect. You're going to object against taking out a small part and you want a large latitude. Okay. We'll find out, because we'll -- first of all, I've got no idea what the paragraph says, not what the ten pages says, not what the 138 pages say. That means that we'll -- first, we will cautiously go step by step. Mr. Jordash has only one step to make. That's one paragraph. You may want to go in other areas and then we'll again and again look at what we're talking about, whether there's any contextualisation, or whether you go somewhere while out of what is even reasonable to be dealt with in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that's a matter that is subject to interpretation. And -- but you're asking the witness to comment on something whether it is consistent or not consistent with that particular aspect [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking the witness anything until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing I asked him is to read 138 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The problem, Your Honour, is that the document, the report, the analysis relates to events in 1995. And he is being asked to be commenting on agreement of a portion of report in -- for events in 1992 and I can't to another portion of that without discussing events in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll proceed very cautiously. If any comment is asked on one paragraph, Mr. Jordash will first of all give the Chamber a possibility to read that paragraph so that we know what we're talking about. We'll cautiously proceed. I've clearly on my mind what your objections are, Mr. Weber. As you may have noticed from the response of the Chamber by the opening statements, that we carefully listen to you but we don't want to rule already at a moment where we do not even know what we are ruling on yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I can indicate for Mr. Theunens' ease that the issue is whether the JNA were involved in the takeover on the 8th of April, 1992. And it's Mr. Butler's view that they were and that issues relating to that is what we want Mr. Theunens to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber has a whole weekend to think about it. You provide the material. We have not heard Mr. Bakrac yet on the matter. Mr. Bakrac, anything you would like to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, I don't wish to take part in this debate. I leave it to you for your assessment, if you allow me another moment, if Mr. Theunens thought that he would leave this courtroom with only 130 pages to read over the weekend, I guess he was wrong. I'm going to ask you for something else now. I have prepared the documents that we would like to use as of Monday. In order for us to carry out preparations properly, we have our documents on CD. Could you please give me your guidance on this. If necessary, we can print hard copies tomorrow. We will cautiously first deal with those documents that have been translated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How many pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say now, Your Honour. I have not instructed my assistant to actually do the word count. We have been so busy. But I think it is about 200 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me, first of all, I think you owe an apology to all those who are assisting us to raise this matter at ten minutes past 7.00. Let me be clear on that. You should have raised it -- you sent a copy to the -- you should have sent a message to Chamber's staff, We want to raise, we have this and this and this we would very much like Mr. Theunens to read. That's not appropriately done at ten minutes past 7.00, Mr. Bakrac. Let that be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Having considered the matter with our team we would abandon the Butler point and we don't ask Mr. Theunens to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Theunens, instead of 138 pages, 200 pages from the Simatovic Defence team, would be you willing to put an eye on it, would you take car care -- I take it that you have a laptop somewhere so you can read it from the screen --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I prefer electronically. It is faster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Exactly. Mr. Bakrac, quick response. Mr. Theunens is willing to look at your material.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you to Mr. Theunens. Thank you to you. I do apologise to all in the courtroom. My intention was, of course, not to keep the staff after 7.00 tonight, but I also didn't want to take any time from my colleague Mr. Jordash of the time he had for cross-examination. Of course, we could have dealt with it earlier. I do apologise to all once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the advantage of sending -- sending an e-mail. Then it doesn't take anyone's time. Mr. Weber, could I really urge you to not spend one more than absolutely necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to put on the record that we're still receiving notification of Simatovic documents at 6.15 this evening. At this time we presume that notification is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether that presumption is right or not will be decided on Monday. We -- I add my apologies and the Chamber's apologies to all those who are suffering under the -- going over the time-limits. We -- let me just see ... one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn until Monday, the 1st of November, quarter past 2.00 in a courtroom which I cannot find at this moment. But one of the three courtrooms in this building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of November, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.15 p.m.,
